instructions: This is a closed-note evaluation designed to check your understanding of Lab 01 (Positron, objects, data types, and data structures). questions.question:
You close Positron and reopen it the next day. R says could not find function when you try a tidyverse function. Which ONE of these two lines must be run again, and in one sentence, why does the OTHER one not need it?

    install.packages("tidyverse")
    library(tidyverse)
questions.answer: library(tidyverse) must be run again. install.packages() wrote the package to the computer's disk, which persists after Positron closes; library() loads it into the session's memory, which is wiped every time the session ends. (Install once per computer; library once per session.)
questions.rubric: 2 pts for naming library(tidyverse) as the line to re-run (0 pts for install.packages, 'both', or 'neither'). 2 pts for the reason: install saves to disk / persists, while library loads into the session / memory that is lost when Positron closes — accept 'once per computer vs once per session' or the drill/garage analogy. 1 pt for a partial reason (e.g. 'library loads it' with no mention of disk/memory or session).
questions.instructor_notes: Lab 01 Q4; Fnd 01 LM9 (install = buying the drill; library = taking it out of the garage). Lab 01 Quiz Q3.

questions.question:
In Lab 01 you ran the two lines below. (a) What number does the second line return? (b) What is R treating each TRUE as when it adds them up?

    test_scores <- c(88, 92, NA, 75, NA, 100)
    sum(is.na(test_scores))
questions.answer: (a) 2. (b) Each TRUE counts as 1 (and FALSE as 0), so the sum is the number of missing values.
questions.rubric: 2 pts for (a) = 2 (0 pts otherwise). 2 pts for (b) TRUE = 1 / FALSE = 0 (accept 'TRUE counts as one'). 1 pt for (b) if the student says is.na() 'finds the NAs' but never says TRUE is counted as 1.
questions.instructor_notes: Lab 01 Q7; Fnd 02 LM5 (is.na + sum idiom). Lab 01 Quiz Q6–Q7.

questions.question: In Lab 01 you typed c("a", 1) in the Console. (a) Write exactly what R printed. (b) In one sentence, why did that happen to the 1?
questions.answer: (a) "a" "1" — a character vector of length 2. (b) A vector holds only ONE type, so R coerced the number to text (the type that can hold both values).
questions.rubric: 2 pts for (a) — "a" "1" with the 1 in quotes (accept 'the 1 became text / a string'; 1 pt if the student says 'a character vector' without showing the output; 0 pts for 'an error' or 'a list'). 2 pts for (b) — a vector holds one type / R coerces everything to character (accept the word 'coercion' alone as full credit). 1 pt for 'it became a character' with no reason.
questions.instructor_notes: Lab 01 Q12 (👀 check) and Fnd 02 Q5 (coercion). Lab 01 Quiz Q9.
